newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Salomons see Philippine 1996-1998 GDP up strongly.
newsitem.headline: Salomons see Philippine 1996-1998 GDP up strongly.

text.p: The Philippines' gross domestic product (GDP) will rise 5.5 percent this year and expand by six percent in 1997 and 6.5 percent in 1998, a report by Salomon Brothers said.
The Weekly Pacific Perspective report of Salomons made available on Sunday said prospects for the Philippine economy in 1997 and beyond remained encouraging.

Strong growth coupled with "a good track record of economic fiscal reform and deregulation in 1996, falling inflation and the prospects of a reduction in interest rates in the near future have created an attractive economic environment for domestic and foreign investors," it said.

"The sustainability of the GDP growth rate will ultimately depend on strong investment growth, as this will also help maintain external competitiveness and, hence, strong export growth," the report added.

The Philippine government recently announced that the country's gross national product (GNP) expanded by 7.1 percent in the first nine months of this year from 5.3 percent over the same period in 1995.
